result.title: MolReJev: Decision Models Are In-Context Molecular Predictors
result.summary: Molecular prediction helps prioritize compounds for screening. Specialized predictors are trained for a fixed set of tasks, limiting cross-task generalization. Language models can condition on task descriptions and have recently shown promise in molecular prediction. However, generating answers token by token adds inference cost, and general-purpose models often lack task-specific molecular knowledge. We thus propose MolReJev, which combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning (ICL) on a language model. MolReJev retrieves similar labeled examples from existing task data and scores candidate labels jointly in one forward pass. ICL improves predictions from the released general-purpose Kev checkpoint and the separately trained MolReJev. For the trained model, gains span all evaluation groups, including held-out tasks, and extend to compounds absent from training. MolReJev generally outperforms MolecularGPT on matched evaluations and nearest-neighbor prediction with the same examples. With four examples, MolReJev and a trained text baseline achieve similar ROC-AUC, with higher measured throughput for MolReJev. These results show that decision models can serve as in-context molecular predictors for compounds, drug pairs, and reactions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MolReJev，把 Jev 式候选打分与 in-context learning 结合用于分子预测：检索相似的已标注样例作为上下文，在一次前向中联合为候选标签打分，以替代逐 token 生成，并在跨任务与未见化合物上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 用单次前向对候选联合打分而非自回归逐 token 生成，可能为 LVR 中并行答案打分、latent 读出与推理成本对比提供方法线索；检索样例构造上下文也供核查「证据筛选」的类比，但原文无视觉或多模态推理实验。
